content:
Earlier in June, we already flagged three cases of US-sanctioned Russian banks bypassing review to get their client apps listed on the App Store. Two months later, a new example has appeared — and it has shot straight to the top of the iPhone App Store download chart.

The latest case is K8CHEN PRO. On the App Store, it is packaged as an app that uses augmented reality (AR) features to help you design your kitchen.

However, the moment you open the app, the disguise immediately falls apart. The privacy policy linked on the App Store is generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator" — that alone is suspicious enough.

In short, this app is definitely a client for T-Bank. What puzzles me most is why this type of app keeps getting through the App Store review mechanism.

When they climb the App Store charts because of all the attention, it's obvious that these are apps that simply should not be there. The situation is quite intriguing.

The two cases from June can be revisited here and here.

Update: As expected, the app has been removed from the App Store.
